0.1.0.title: First release - build an app out of panels
notes: First public build of XENO Apps. It is an experimental, unsigned release for Windows: SmartScreen will show "Windows protected your PC" - choose More info, then Run anyway.

Compose an app from 21 first-party panels - table, chart, metrics, tree, fields, calendar, connectors, inspector, layers, history, transport, viewport, console, runs, terminal, diff, find, comments, consent, account and color.
FRONT and BACK are two projections of one graph. FRONT is the working app; BACK is the same app as a node canvas. BACK draws over FRONT rather than replacing it, so the two views cannot disagree.
Wire panels together by dragging between pins on the BACK canvas, in either direction, snapping only to type-compatible ports - or through the Wiring panel in FRONT.
Eight logic nodes for the steps that belong to no panel: expression, map, filter, text-formatter, json-transform, if-else, switch and code.
Real data: HTTP and GraphQL endpoints, CSV and JSON files, and pasted-in rows. Requests are made from the main process, so cross-origin rules are not a constraint.

Network access is per-origin and consented before a socket opens - an unapproved host is unreachable, not filtered after the fact, and a damaged consent store fails closed. Review grants in File, Permissions.
Credentials are stored in the OS keystore and referenced as $cred:<id>. There is deliberately no channel that reads a secret back out, and nothing is written into your .xapp.
Place the same panel more than once - each instance carries its own configuration and state.
Authoring undo and redo across wires, logic nodes, placement, instances and configuration.
Run-on-open triggers, so a saved app shows data as soon as it opens instead of restoring an empty layout. Triggers are validated against each panel's declared commands.
Five starter templates - support desk dashboard, records and detail, service monitor, review workspace, and blank - built through the same API you drive by hand.
Save and reopen a single .xapp: indented JSON carrying the composition only, with panels referenced by manifest id rather than embedded. No credentials and no absolute paths are written into it.

Panel Studio: write your own panel and run it in an opaque-origin iframe with no network, no filesystem and no GPU. Local storage is the one grantable capability. It is a plain iframe rather than a JS isolate, so a runaway loop hangs that frame.

Known limits in this release: there is no AI - no model is called anywhere in this build. There is no way to publish, share or export a built app; you save a local .xapp. There is no auto-update, so a new version means downloading it again. There are no SQL or database sources, and no execution wires, which means no retry, checkpointing or execution-order guarantee. The Terminal panel is a scripted emulator, not a shell. Windows only - macOS and Linux are configured but not built.
Verified by 428 unit tests and a 36-gate harness that drives the real application in a real window, including against the packaged build.
